For example, this could represent an employee's salary over a specific period of time. __Note:__ This type has been superseded by [[MonetaryAmount]], use of that type is recommended. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [DayOfWeek](http://schema.org/DayOfWeek) | class | The day of the week, e.g. used to specify to which day the opening hours of an OpeningHoursSpecification refer.<br><br>Originally, URLs from [GoodRelations](http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1) were used (for [[Monday]], [[Tuesday]], [[Wednesday]], [[Thursday]], [[Friday]], [[Saturday]], [[Sunday]] plus a special entry for [[PublicHolidays]]); these have now been integrated directly into schema.org.<br> |
| `http://schema.org/` | [DaySpa](http://schema.org/DaySpa) | class | A day spa. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [DeactivateAction](http://schema.org/DeactivateAction) | class | The act of stopping or deactivating a device or application (e.g. stopping a timer or turning off a flashlight). |
| `http://schema.org/` | [DefenceEstablishment](http://schema.org/DefenceEstablishment) | class | A defence establishment, such as an army or navy base. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [DefinedRegion](http://schema.org/DefinedRegion) | class | A DefinedRegion is a geographic area defined by potentially arbitrary (rather than political, administrative or natural geographical) criteria. Properties are provided for defining a region by reference to sets of postal codes.<br><br>Examples: a delivery destination when shopping. Region where regional pricing is configured.<br><br>Requirement 1:<br>Country: US<br>States: "NY", "CA"<br><br>Requirement 2:<br>Country: US<br>PostalCode Set: { [94000-94585], [97000, 97999], [13000, 13599]}<br>{ [12345, 12345], [78945, 78945], }<br>Region = state, canton, prefecture, autonomous community...<br> |
| `http://schema.org/` | [DefinedTerm](http://schema.org/DefinedTerm) | class | A word, name, acronym, phrase, etc. with a formal definition. Often used in the context of category or subject classification, glossaries or dictionaries, product or creative work types, etc. Use the name property for the term being defined, use termCode if the term has an alpha-numeric code allocated, use description to provide the definition of the term. Use the about property to specify what the term is about. |

| `http://schema.org/` | [DeleteAction](http://schema.org/DeleteAction) | class | The act of editing a recipient by removing one of its objects. |

| `http://schema.org/` | [DeliveryMethod](http://schema.org/DeliveryMethod) | class | A delivery method is a standardized procedure for transferring the product or service to the destination of fulfillment chosen by the customer. Delivery methods are characterized by the means of transportation used, and by the organization or group that is the contracting party for the sending organization or person.\n\nCommonly used values:\n\n* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#DeliveryModeDirectDownload\n* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#DeliveryModeFreight\n* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#DeliveryModeMail\n* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#DeliveryModeOwnFleet\n* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#DeliveryModePickUp\n* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#DHL\n* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#FederalExpress\n* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#UPS<br> |
| `http://schema.org/` | [Demand](http://schema.org/Demand) | class | A demand entity represents the public, not necessarily binding, not necessarily exclusive, announcement by an organization or person to seek a certain type of goods or services. For describing demand using this type, the very same properties used for Offer apply. |

| `http://schema.org/` | [DepartmentStore](http://schema.org/DepartmentStore) | class | A department store. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [DepositAccount](http://schema.org/DepositAccount) | class | A type of Bank Account with a main purpose of depositing funds to gain interest or other benefits. |

| `http://schema.org/` | [DigitalPlatformEnumeration](http://schema.org/DigitalPlatformEnumeration) | class | Enumerates some common technology platforms, for use with properties such as [[actionPlatform]]. It is not supposed to be comprehensive - when a suitable code is not enumerated here, textual or URL values can be used instead. These codes are at a fairly high level and do not deal with versioning and other nuance. Additional codes can be suggested [in github](https://github.com/schemaorg/schemaorg/issues/3057). |
| `http://schema.org/` | [DisagreeAction](http://schema.org/DisagreeAction) | class | The act of expressing a difference of opinion with the object. An agent disagrees to/about an object (a proposition, topic or theme) with participants. |

| `http://schema.org/` | [DrinkAction](http://schema.org/DrinkAction) | class | The act of swallowing liquids. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [DriveWheelConfigurationValue](http://schema.org/DriveWheelConfigurationValue) | class | A value indicating which roadwheels will receive torque. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [Drug](http://schema.org/Drug) | class | A chemical or biologic substance, used as a medical therapy, that has a physiological effect on an organism. Here the term drug is used interchangeably with the term medicine although clinical knowledge makes a clear difference between them. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [DrugClass](http://schema.org/DrugClass) | class | A class of medical drugs, e.g., statins. Classes can represent general pharmacological class, common mechanisms of action, common physiological effects, etc. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [DrugCost](http://schema.org/DrugCost) | class | The cost per unit of a medical drug. Costs of medical drugs vary widely depending on how and where they are paid for, so while this type captures some of the variables, costs should be used with caution by consumers of this schema's markup. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [DrugCostCategory](http://schema.org/DrugCostCategory) | class | Enumerated categories of medical drug costs. |

| `http://schema.org/` | [EndorsementRating](http://schema.org/EndorsementRating) | class | An EndorsementRating is a rating that expresses some level of endorsement, for example inclusion in a "critic's pick" blog, a<br>"Like" or "+1" on a social network. It can be considered the [[result]] of an [[EndorseAction]] in which the [[object]] of the action is rated positively by<br>some [[agent]]. As is common elsewhere in schema.org, it is sometimes more useful to describe the results of such an action without explicitly describing the [[Action]].<br><br>An [[EndorsementRating]] may be part of a numeric scale or organized system, but this is not required: having an explicit type for indicating a positive,<br>endorsement rating is particularly useful in the absence of numeric scales as it helps consumers understand that the rating is broadly positive.<br> |
| `http://schema.org/` | [Energy](http://schema.org/Energy) | class | Properties that take Energy as values are of the form '&lt;Number&gt; &lt;Energy unit of measure&gt;'. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [EnergyConsumptionDetails](http://schema.org/EnergyConsumptionDetails) | class | EnergyConsumptionDetails represents information related to the energy efficiency of a product that consumes energy. The information that can be provided is based on international regulations such as for example [EU directive 2017/1369](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2017/1369/oj) for energy labeling and the [Energy labeling rule](https://www.ftc.gov/enforcement/rules/rulemaking-regulatory-reform-proceedings/energy-water-use-labeling-consumer) under the Energy Policy and Conservation Act (EPCA) in the US. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [EnergyEfficiencyEnumeration](http://schema.org/EnergyEfficiencyEnumeration) | class | Enumerates energy efficiency levels (also known as "classes" or "ratings") and certifications that are part of several international energy efficiency standards. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [EnergyStarEnergyEfficiencyEnumeration](http://schema.org/EnergyStarEnergyEfficiencyEnumeration) | class | Used to indicate whether a product is EnergyStar certified. |

| `http://schema.org/` | [EntryPoint](http://schema.org/EntryPoint) | class | An entry point, within some Web-based protocol. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [Enumeration](http://schema.org/Enumeration) | class | Lists or enumerations—for example, a list of cuisines or music genres, etc. |

| `http://schema.org/` | [Error](http://schema.org/Error) | class | Representation of an Error. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [Event](http://schema.org/Event) | class | An event happening at a certain time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Ticketing information may be added via the [[offers]] property. Repeated events may be structured as separate Event objects. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [EventAttendanceModeEnumeration](http://schema.org/EventAttendanceModeEnumeration) | class | An EventAttendanceModeEnumeration value is one of potentially several modes of organising an event, relating to whether it is online or offline. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [EventReservation](http://schema.org/EventReservation) | class | A reservation for an event like a concert, sporting event, or lecture.\n\nNote: This type is for information about actual reservations, e.g. in confirmation emails or HTML pages with individual confirmations of reservations. For offers of tickets, use [[Offer]]. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [EventSeries](http://schema.org/EventSeries) | class | A series of [[Event]]s. Included events can relate with the series using the [[superEvent]] property.<br><br>An EventSeries is a collection of events that share some unifying characteristic. For example, "The Olympic Games" is a series, which<br>is repeated regularly. The "2012 London Olympics" can be presented both as an [[Event]] in the series "Olympic Games", and as an<br>[[EventSeries]] that included a number of sporting competitions as Events.<br><br>The nature of the association between the events in an [[EventSeries]] can vary, but typical examples could<br>include a thematic event series (e.g. topical meetups or classes), or a series of regular events that share a location, attendee group and/or organizers.<br><br>EventSeries has been defined as a kind of Event to make it easy for publishers to use it in an Event context without<br>worrying about which kinds of series are really event-like enough to call an Event. In general an EventSeries<br>may seem more Event-like when the period of time is compact and when aspects such as location are fixed, but<br>it may also sometimes prove useful to describe a longer-term series as an Event.<br> |
| `http://schema.org/` | [EventStatusType](http://schema.org/EventStatusType) | class | EventStatusType is an enumeration type whose instances represent several states that an Event may be in. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [EventVenue](http://schema.org/EventVenue) | class | An event venue. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [ExchangeRateSpecification](http://schema.org/ExchangeRateSpecification) | class | A structured value representing exchange rate. |

| `http://schema.org/` | [ExercisePlan](http://schema.org/ExercisePlan) | class | Fitness-related activity designed for a specific health-related purpose, including defined exercise routines as well as activity prescribed by a clinician. |

| `http://schema.org/` | [FinancialIncentive](http://schema.org/FinancialIncentive) | class | <p>Represents financial incentives for goods/services offered by an organization (or individual).</p><br><br><p>Typically contains the [[name]] of the incentive, the [[incentivizedItem]], the [[incentiveAmount]], the [[incentiveStatus]], [[incentiveType]], the [[provider]] of the incentive, and [[eligibleWithSupplier]].</p><br><br><p>Optionally contains criteria on whether the incentive is limited based on [[purchaseType]], [[purchasePriceLimit]], [[incomeLimit]], and the [[qualifiedExpense]].<br> |
| `http://schema.org/` | [FinancialProduct](http://schema.org/FinancialProduct) | class | A product provided to consumers and businesses by financial institutions such as banks, insurance companies, brokerage firms, consumer finance companies, and investment companies which comprise the financial services industry. |

| `http://schema.org/` | [FlightReservation](http://schema.org/FlightReservation) | class | A reservation for air travel.\n\nNote: This type is for information about actual reservations, e.g. in confirmation emails or HTML pages with individual confirmations of reservations. For offers of tickets, use [[Offer]]. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [Float](http://schema.org/Float) | class | Data type: Floating number. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [FloorPlan](http://schema.org/FloorPlan) | class | A FloorPlan is an explicit representation of a collection of similar accommodations, allowing the provision of common information (room counts, sizes, layout diagrams) and offers for rental or sale. In typical use, some [[ApartmentComplex]] has an [[accommodationFloorPlan]] which is a [[FloorPlan]]. A FloorPlan is always in the context of a particular place, either a larger [[ApartmentComplex]] or a single [[Apartment]]. The visual/spatial aspects of a floor plan (i.e. room layout, [see wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Floor_plan)) can be indicated using [[image]]. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [Florist](http://schema.org/Florist) | class | A florist. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [FollowAction](http://schema.org/FollowAction) | class | The act of forming a personal connection with someone/something (object) unidirectionally/asymmetrically to get updates polled from.\n\nRelated actions:\n\n* [[BefriendAction]]: Unlike BefriendAction, FollowAction implies that the connection is *not* necessarily reciprocal.\n* [[SubscribeAction]]: Unlike SubscribeAction, FollowAction implies that the follower acts as an active agent constantly/actively polling for updates.\n* [[RegisterAction]]: Unlike RegisterAction, FollowAction implies that the agent is interested in continuing receiving updates from the object.\n* [[JoinAction]]: Unlike JoinAction, FollowAction implies that the agent is interested in getting updates from the object.\n* [[TrackAction]]: Unlike TrackAction, FollowAction refers to the polling of updates of all aspects of animate objects rather than the location of inanimate objects (e.g. you track a package, but you don't follow it). |
| `http://schema.org/` | [FoodEstablishment](http://schema.org/FoodEstablishment) | class | A food-related business. |

| `http://schema.org/` | [FundingAgency](http://schema.org/FundingAgency) | class | A FundingAgency is an organization that implements one or more [[FundingScheme]]s and manages<br>the granting process (via [[Grant]]s, typically [[MonetaryGrant]]s).<br>A funding agency is not always required for grant funding, e.g. philanthropic giving, corporate sponsorship etc.<br><br>Examples of funding agencies include ERC, REA, NIH, Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation, ...<br> |
| `http://schema.org/` | [FundingScheme](http://schema.org/FundingScheme) | class | A FundingScheme combines organizational, project and policy aspects of grant-based funding<br>that sets guidelines, principles and mechanisms to support other kinds of projects and activities.<br>Funding is typically organized via [[Grant]] funding. Examples of funding schemes: Swiss Priority Programmes (SPPs); EU Framework 7 (FP7); Horizon 2020; the NIH-R01 Grant Program; Wellcome institutional strategic support fund. For large scale public sector funding, the management and administration of grant awards is often handled by other, dedicated, organizations - [[FundingAgency]]s such as ERC, REA, ... |
| `http://schema.org/` | [FurnitureStore](http://schema.org/FurnitureStore) | class | A furniture store. |

Examples include FOXP2 (Forkhead box protein P2), SCARNA21 (small Cajal body-specific RNA 21), A- (agouti genotype). |

| `http://schema.org/` | [GeoCircle](http://schema.org/GeoCircle) | class | A GeoCircle is a GeoShape representing a circular geographic area. As it is a GeoShape<br>it provides the simple textual property 'circle', but also allows the combination of postalCode alongside geoRadius.<br>The center of the circle can be indicated via the 'geoMidpoint' property, or more approximately using 'address', 'postalCode'.<br> |

| `http://schema.org/` | [Grant](http://schema.org/Grant) | class | A grant, typically financial or otherwise quantifiable, of resources. Typically a [[funder]] sponsors some [[MonetaryAmount]] to an [[Organization]] or [[Person]],<br>sometimes not necessarily via a dedicated or long-lived [[Project]], resulting in one or more outputs, or [[fundedItem]]s. For financial sponsorship, indicate the [[funder]] of a [[MonetaryGrant]]. For non-financial support, indicate [[sponsor]] of [[Grant]]s of resources (e.g. office space).<br><br>Grants support activities directed towards some agreed collective goals, often but not always organized as [[Project]]s. Long-lived projects are sometimes sponsored by a variety of grants over time, but it is also common for a project to be associated with a single grant.<br><br>The amount of a [[Grant]] is represented using [[amount]] as a [[MonetaryAmount]].<br> |

A [[Guide]] may represent a Buying Guide and detail aspects of products or services for a user to consider. A [[Guide]] may represent a Product Guide and recommend specific products or services. A [[Guide]] may represent a Ranked List and recommend specific products or services with ranking. |

| `http://schema.org/` | [HealthClub](http://schema.org/HealthClub) | class | A health club. |

Multiple instances of [[WebContent]] (and hence [[HealthTopicContent]]) can be related using [[hasPart]] / [[isPartOf]] where there is some kind of content hierarchy, and their content described with [[about]] and [[mentions]] e.g. building upon the existing [[MedicalCondition]] vocabulary.<br> |

| `http://schema.org/` | [Hostel](http://schema.org/Hostel) | class | A hostel - cheap accommodation, often in shared dormitories.<br><br /><br /><br>See also the <a href="/docs/hotels.html">dedicated document on the use of schema.org for marking up hotels and other forms of accommodations</a>.<br> |
| `http://schema.org/` | [Hotel](http://schema.org/Hotel) | class | A hotel is an establishment that provides lodging paid on a short-term basis (source: Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia, see http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hotel).<br><br /><br /><br>See also the <a href="/docs/hotels.html">dedicated document on the use of schema.org for marking up hotels and other forms of accommodations</a>.<br> |
| `http://schema.org/` | [HotelRoom](http://schema.org/HotelRoom) | class | A hotel room is a single room in a hotel.<br><br /><br /><br>See also the <a href="/docs/hotels.html">dedicated document on the use of schema.org for marking up hotels and other forms of accommodations</a>.<br> |
| `http://schema.org/` | [House](http://schema.org/House) | class | A house is a building or structure that has the ability to be occupied for habitation by humans or other creatures (source: Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia, see <a href="http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House">http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House</a>). |
| `http://schema.org/` | [HousePainter](http://schema.org/HousePainter) | class | A house painting service. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [HowTo](http://schema.org/HowTo) | class | Instructions that explain how to achieve a result by performing a sequence of steps. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [HowToDirection](http://schema.org/HowToDirection) | class | A direction indicating a single action to do in the instructions for how to achieve a result. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [HowToItem](http://schema.org/HowToItem) | class | An item used as either a tool or supply when performing the instructions for how to achieve a result. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [HowToSection](http://schema.org/HowToSection) | class | A sub-grouping of steps in the instructions for how to achieve a result (e.g. steps for making a pie crust within a pie recipe). |
| `http://schema.org/` | [HowToStep](http://schema.org/HowToStep) | class | A step in the instructions for how to achieve a result. It is an ordered list with HowToDirection and/or HowToTip items. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [HowToSupply](http://schema.org/HowToSupply) | class | A supply consumed when performing the instructions for how to achieve a result. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [HowToTip](http://schema.org/HowToTip) | class | An explanation in the instructions for how to achieve a result. It provides supplementary information about a technique, supply, author's preference, etc. It can explain what could be done, or what should not be done, but doesn't specify what should be done (see HowToDirection). |
| `http://schema.org/` | [HowToTool](http://schema.org/HowToTool) | class | A tool used (but not consumed) when performing instructions for how to achieve a result. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [HyperToc](http://schema.org/HyperToc) | class | A HyperToc represents a hypertext table of contents for complex media objects, such as [[VideoObject]], [[AudioObject]]. Items in the table of contents are indicated using the [[tocEntry]] property, and typed [[HyperTocEntry]]. For cases where the same larger work is split into multiple files, [[associatedMedia]] can be used on individual [[HyperTocEntry]] items. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [HyperTocEntry](http://schema.org/HyperTocEntry) | class | A HyperToEntry is an item within a [[HyperToc]], which represents a hypertext table of contents for complex media objects, such as [[VideoObject]], [[AudioObject]]. The media object itself is indicated using [[associatedMedia]]. Each section of interest within that content can be described with a [[HyperTocEntry]], with associated [[startOffset]] and [[endOffset]]. When several entries are all from the same file, [[associatedMedia]] is used on the overarching [[HyperTocEntry]]; if the content has been split into multiple files, they can be referenced using [[associatedMedia]] on each [[HyperTocEntry]]. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [IPTCDigitalSourceEnumeration](http://schema.org/IPTCDigitalSourceEnumeration) | class | <a href="https://www.iptc.org/">IPTC</a> "Digital Source" codes for use with the [[digitalSourceType]] property, providing information about the source for a digital media object.<br>In general these codes are not declared here to be mutually exclusive, although some combinations would be contradictory if applied simultaneously, or might be considered mutually incompatible by upstream maintainers of the definitions. See the IPTC <a href="https://www.iptc.org/std/photometadata/documentation/userguide/">documentation</a><br>for <a href="https://cv.iptc.org/newscodes/digitalsourcetype/">detailed definitions</a> of all terms. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [IceCreamShop](http://schema.org/IceCreamShop) | class | An ice cream shop. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [IgnoreAction](http://schema.org/IgnoreAction) | class | The act of intentionally disregarding the object. An agent ignores an object. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [ImageGallery](http://schema.org/ImageGallery) | class | Web page type: Image gallery page. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [ImageObject](http://schema.org/ImageObject) | class | An image file. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [ImageObjectSnapshot](http://schema.org/ImageObjectSnapshot) | class | A specific and exact (byte-for-byte) version of an [[ImageObject]]. Two byte-for-byte identical files, for the purposes of this type, considered identical. If they have different embedded metadata (e.g. XMP, EXIF) the files will differ. Different external facts about the files, e.g. creator or dateCreated that aren't represented in their actual content, do not affect this notion of identity. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [ImagingTest](http://schema.org/ImagingTest) | class | Any medical imaging modality typically used for diagnostic purposes. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [IncentiveQualifiedExpenseType](http://schema.org/IncentiveQualifiedExpenseType) | class | The types of expenses that are covered by the incentive. For example some incentives are only for the goods (tangible items) but the services (labor) are excluded. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [IncentiveStatus](http://schema.org/IncentiveStatus) | class | Enumerates a status for an incentive, such as whether it is active. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [IncentiveType](http://schema.org/IncentiveType) | class | Enumerates common financial incentives for products, including tax credits, tax deductions, rebates and subsidies, etc. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [IndividualPhysician](http://schema.org/IndividualPhysician) | class | An individual medical practitioner. For their official address use [[address]], for affiliations to hospitals use [[hospitalAffiliation]].<br>The [[practicesAt]] property can be used to indicate [[MedicalOrganization]] hospitals, clinics, pharmacies etc. where this physician practices. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [IndividualProduct](http://schema.org/IndividualProduct) | class | A single, identifiable product instance (e.g. a laptop with a particular serial number). |
| `http://schema.org/` | [InfectiousAgentClass](http://schema.org/InfectiousAgentClass) | class | Classes of agents or pathogens that transmit infectious diseases. Enumerated type. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [InfectiousDisease](http://schema.org/InfectiousDisease) | class | An infectious disease is a clinically evident human disease resulting from the presence of pathogenic microbial agents, like pathogenic viruses, pathogenic bacteria, fungi, protozoa, multicellular parasites, and prions. To be considered an infectious disease, such pathogens are known to be able to cause this disease. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [InformAction](http://schema.org/InformAction) | class | The act of notifying someone of information pertinent to them, with no expectation of a response. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [InsertAction](http://schema.org/InsertAction) | class | The act of adding at a specific location in an ordered collection. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [InstallAction](http://schema.org/InstallAction) | class | The act of installing an application. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [InstantaneousEvent](http://schema.org/InstantaneousEvent) | class | An event with no duration, like for instance a computer log entry. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [InsuranceAgency](http://schema.org/InsuranceAgency) | class | An Insurance agency. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [Intangible](http://schema.org/Intangible) | class | A utility class that serves as the umbrella for a number of 'intangible' things such as quantities, structured values, etc. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [Integer](http://schema.org/Integer) | class | Data type: Integer. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [InteractAction](http://schema.org/InteractAction) | class | The act of interacting with another person or organization. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [InteractionCounter](http://schema.org/InteractionCounter) | class | A summary of how users have interacted with this CreativeWork. In most cases, authors will use a subtype to specify the specific type of interaction. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [InternetCafe](http://schema.org/InternetCafe) | class | An internet cafe. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [InvestmentFund](http://schema.org/InvestmentFund) | class | A company or fund that gathers capital from a number of investors to create a pool of money that is then re-invested into stocks, bonds and other assets. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [InvestmentOrDeposit](http://schema.org/InvestmentOrDeposit) | class | A type of financial product that typically requires the client to transfer funds to a financial service in return for potential beneficial financial return. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [InviteAction](http://schema.org/InviteAction) | class | The act of asking someone to attend an event. Reciprocal of RsvpAction. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [Invoice](http://schema.org/Invoice) | class | A statement of the money due for goods or services; a bill. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [ItemAvailability](http://schema.org/ItemAvailability) | class | A list of possible product availability options. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [ItemList](http://schema.org/ItemList) | class | A list of items of any sort&#x2014;for example, Top 10 Movies About Weathermen, or Top 100 Party Songs. Not to be confused with HTML lists, which are often used only for formatting. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [ItemListOrderType](http://schema.org/ItemListOrderType) | class | Enumerated for values for itemListOrder for indicating how an ordered ItemList is organized. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [ItemPage](http://schema.org/ItemPage) | class | A page devoted to a single item, such as a particular product or hotel. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [JewelryStore](http://schema.org/JewelryStore) | class | A jewelry store. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [JobPosting](http://schema.org/JobPosting) | class | A listing that describes a job opening in a certain organization. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [JoinAction](http://schema.org/JoinAction) | class | An agent joins an event/group with participants/friends at a location.\n\nRelated actions:\n\n* [[RegisterAction]]: Unlike RegisterAction, JoinAction refers to joining a group/team of people.\n* [[SubscribeAction]]: Unlike SubscribeAction, JoinAction does not imply that you'll be receiving updates.\n* [[FollowAction]]: Unlike FollowAction, JoinAction does not imply that you'll be polling for updates. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [Joint](http://schema.org/Joint) | class | The anatomical location at which two or more bones make contact. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [LakeBodyOfWater](http://schema.org/LakeBodyOfWater) | class | A lake (for example, Lake Pontrachain). |
| `http://schema.org/` | [Landform](http://schema.org/Landform) | class | A landform or physical feature. Landform elements include mountains, plains, lakes, rivers, seascape and oceanic waterbody interface features such as bays, peninsulas, seas and so forth, including sub-aqueous terrain features such as submersed mountain ranges, volcanoes, and the great ocean basins. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [LandmarksOrHistoricalBuildings](http://schema.org/LandmarksOrHistoricalBuildings) | class | An historical landmark or building. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [Language](http://schema.org/Language) | class | Natural languages such as Spanish, Tamil, Hindi, English, etc. Formal language code tags expressed in [BCP 47](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IETF_language_tag) can be used via the [[alternateName]] property. The Language type previously also covered programming languages such as Scheme and Lisp, which are now best represented using [[ComputerLanguage]]. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [LearningResource](http://schema.org/LearningResource) | class | The LearningResource type can be used to indicate [[CreativeWork]]s (whether physical or digital) that have a particular and explicit orientation towards learning, education, skill acquisition, and other educational purposes.<br><br>[[LearningResource]] is expected to be used as an addition to a primary type such as [[Book]], [[VideoObject]], [[Product]] etc.<br><br>[[EducationEvent]] serves a similar purpose for event-like things (e.g. a [[Trip]]). A [[LearningResource]] may be created as a result of an [[EducationEvent]], for example by recording one. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [LeaveAction](http://schema.org/LeaveAction) | class | An agent leaves an event / group with participants/friends at a location.\n\nRelated actions:\n\n* [[JoinAction]]: The antonym of LeaveAction.\n* [[UnRegisterAction]]: Unlike UnRegisterAction, LeaveAction implies leaving a group/team of people rather than a service. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [LegalForceStatus](http://schema.org/LegalForceStatus) | class | A list of possible statuses for the legal force of a legislation. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [LegalService](http://schema.org/LegalService) | class | A LegalService is a business that provides legally-oriented services, advice and representation, e.g. law firms.\n\nAs a [[LocalBusiness]] it can be described as a [[provider]] of one or more [[Service]]\(s). |
| `http://schema.org/` | [LegalValueLevel](http://schema.org/LegalValueLevel) | class | A list of possible levels for the legal validity of a legislation. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [Legislation](http://schema.org/Legislation) | class | A legal document such as an act, decree, bill, etc. (enforceable or not) or a component of a legal act (like an article). |
| `http://schema.org/` | [LegislationObject](http://schema.org/LegislationObject) | class | A specific object or file containing a Legislation. Note that the same Legislation can be published in multiple files. For example, a digitally signed PDF, a plain PDF and an HTML version. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [LegislativeBuilding](http://schema.org/LegislativeBuilding) | class | A legislative building&#x2014;for example, the state capitol. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [LendAction](http://schema.org/LendAction) | class | The act of providing an object under an agreement that it will be returned at a later date. Reciprocal of BorrowAction.\n\nRelated actions:\n\n* [[BorrowAction]]: Reciprocal of LendAction. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [Library](http://schema.org/Library) | class | A library. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [LibrarySystem](http://schema.org/LibrarySystem) | class | A [[LibrarySystem]] is a collaborative system amongst several libraries. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [LifestyleModification](http://schema.org/LifestyleModification) | class | A process of care involving exercise, changes to diet, fitness routines, and other lifestyle changes aimed at improving a health condition. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [Ligament](http://schema.org/Ligament) | class | A short band of tough, flexible, fibrous connective tissue that functions to connect multiple bones, cartilages, and structurally support joints. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [LikeAction](http://schema.org/LikeAction) | class | The act of expressing a positive sentiment about the object. An agent likes an object (a proposition, topic or theme) with participants. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [LinkRole](http://schema.org/LinkRole) | class | A Role that represents a Web link, e.g. as expressed via the 'url' property. Its linkRelationship property can indicate URL-based and plain textual link types, e.g. those in IANA link registry or others such as 'amphtml'. This structure provides a placeholder where details from HTML's link element can be represented outside of HTML, e.g. in JSON-LD feeds. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [LiquorStore](http://schema.org/LiquorStore) | class | A shop that sells alcoholic drinks such as wine, beer, whisky and other spirits. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [ListItem](http://schema.org/ListItem) | class | An list item, e.g. a step in a checklist or how-to description. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [ListenAction](http://schema.org/ListenAction) | class | The act of consuming audio content. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [LiteraryEvent](http://schema.org/LiteraryEvent) | class | Event type: Literary event. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [LiveBlogPosting](http://schema.org/LiveBlogPosting) | class | A [[LiveBlogPosting]] is a [[BlogPosting]] intended to provide a rolling textual coverage of an ongoing event through continuous updates. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [LoanOrCredit](http://schema.org/LoanOrCredit) | class | A financial product for the loaning of an amount of money, or line of credit, under agreed terms and charges. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [LocalBusiness](http://schema.org/LocalBusiness) | class | A particular physical business or branch of an organization. Examples of LocalBusiness include a restaurant, a particular branch of a restaurant chain, a branch of a bank, a medical practice, a club, a bowling alley, etc. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [LocationFeatureSpecification](http://schema.org/LocationFeatureSpecification) | class | Specifies a location feature by providing a structured value representing a feature of an accommodation as a property-value pair of varying degrees of formality. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [Locksmith](http://schema.org/Locksmith) | class | A locksmith. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [LodgingBusiness](http://schema.org/LodgingBusiness) | class | A lodging business, such as a motel, hotel, or inn. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [LodgingReservation](http://schema.org/LodgingReservation) | class | A reservation for lodging at a hotel, motel, inn, etc.\n\nNote: This type is for information about actual reservations, e.g. in confirmation emails or HTML pages with individual confirmations of reservations. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [LoginAction](http://schema.org/LoginAction) | class | The action of logging into a device or application. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [LoseAction](http://schema.org/LoseAction) | class | The act of being defeated in a competitive activity. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [LymphaticVessel](http://schema.org/LymphaticVessel) | class | A type of blood vessel that specifically carries lymph fluid unidirectionally toward the heart. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [Manuscript](http://schema.org/Manuscript) | class | A book, document, or piece of music written by hand rather than typed or printed. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [Map](http://schema.org/Map) | class | A map. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [MapCategoryType](http://schema.org/MapCategoryType) | class | An enumeration of several kinds of Map. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [MarryAction](http://schema.org/MarryAction) | class | The act of marrying a person. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [Mass](http://schema.org/Mass) | class | Properties that take Mass as values are of the form '&lt;Number&gt; &lt;Mass unit of measure&gt;'. E.g., '7 kg'. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [MathSolver](http://schema.org/MathSolver) | class | A math solver which is capable of solving a subset of mathematical problems. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [MaximumDoseSchedule](http://schema.org/MaximumDoseSchedule) | class | The maximum dosing schedule considered safe for a drug or supplement as recommended by an authority or by the drug/supplement's manufacturer. Capture the recommending authority in the recognizingAuthority property of MedicalEntity. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [MeasurementMethodEnum](http://schema.org/MeasurementMethodEnum) | class | Enumeration(s) for use with [[measurementMethod]]. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [MeasurementTypeEnumeration](http://schema.org/MeasurementTypeEnumeration) | class | Enumeration of common measurement types (or dimensions), for example "chest" for a person, "inseam" for pants, "gauge" for screws, or "wheel" for bicycles. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [MediaEnumeration](http://schema.org/MediaEnumeration) | class | MediaEnumeration enumerations are lists of codes, labels etc. useful for describing media objects. They may be reflections of externally developed lists, or created at schema.org, or a combination. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [MediaGallery](http://schema.org/MediaGallery) | class | Web page type: Media gallery page. A mixed-media page that can contain media such as images, videos, and other multimedia. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [MediaManipulationRatingEnumeration](http://schema.org/MediaManipulationRatingEnumeration) | class | Codes for use with the [[mediaAuthenticityCategory]] property, indicating the authenticity of a media object (in the context of how it was published or shared). In general these codes are not mutually exclusive, although some combinations (such as 'original' versus 'transformed', 'edited' and 'staged') would be contradictory if applied in the same [[MediaReview]]. Note that the application of these codes is with regard to a piece of media shared or published in a particular context. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [MediaObject](http://schema.org/MediaObject) | class | A media object, such as an image, video, audio, or text object embedded in a web page or a downloadable dataset i.e. DataDownload. Note that a creative work may have many media objects associated with it on the same web page. For example, a page about a single song (MusicRecording) may have a music video (VideoObject), and a high and low bandwidth audio stream (2 AudioObject's). |
| `http://schema.org/` | [MediaReview](http://schema.org/MediaReview) | class | A [[MediaReview]] is a more specialized form of Review dedicated to the evaluation of media content online, typically in the context of fact-checking and misinformation.<br>For more general reviews of media in the broader sense, use [[UserReview]], [[CriticReview]] or other [[Review]] types. This definition is<br>a work in progress. While the [[MediaManipulationRatingEnumeration]] list reflects significant community review amongst fact-checkers and others working<br>to combat misinformation, the specific structures for representing media objects, their versions and publication context, are still evolving. Similarly, best practices for the relationship between [[MediaReview]] and [[ClaimReview]] markup have not yet been finalized. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [MediaReviewItem](http://schema.org/MediaReviewItem) | class | Represents an item or group of closely related items treated as a unit for the sake of evaluation in a [[MediaReview]]. Authorship etc. apply to the items rather than to the curation/grouping or reviewing party. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [MediaSubscription](http://schema.org/MediaSubscription) | class | A subscription which allows a user to access media including audio, video, books, etc. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [MedicalAudience](http://schema.org/MedicalAudience) | class | Target audiences for medical web pages. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [MedicalAudienceType](http://schema.org/MedicalAudienceType) | class | Target audiences types for medical web pages. Enumerated type. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [MedicalBusiness](http://schema.org/MedicalBusiness) | class | A particular physical or virtual business of an organization for medical purposes. Examples of MedicalBusiness include different businesses run by health professionals. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [MedicalCause](http://schema.org/MedicalCause) | class | The causative agent(s) that are responsible for the pathophysiologic process that eventually results in a medical condition, symptom or sign. In this schema, unless otherwise specified this is meant to be the proximate cause of the medical condition, symptom or sign. The proximate cause is defined as the causative agent that most directly results in the medical condition, symptom or sign. For example, the HIV virus could be considered a cause of AIDS. Or in a diagnostic context, if a patient fell and sustained a hip fracture and two days later sustained a pulmonary embolism which eventuated in a cardiac arrest, the cause of the cardiac arrest (the proximate cause) would be the pulmonary embolism and not the fall. Medical causes can include cardiovascular, chemical, dermatologic, endocrine, environmental, gastroenterologic, genetic, hematologic, gynecologic, iatrogenic, infectious, musculoskeletal, neurologic, nutritional, obstetric, oncologic, otolaryngologic, pharmacologic, psychiatric, pulmonary, renal, rheumatologic, toxic, traumatic, or urologic causes; medical conditions can be causes as well. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [MedicalClinic](http://schema.org/MedicalClinic) | class | A facility, often associated with a hospital or medical school, that is devoted to the specific diagnosis and/or healthcare. Previously limited to outpatients but with evolution it may be open to inpatients as well. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [MedicalCode](http://schema.org/MedicalCode) | class | A code for a medical entity. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [MedicalCondition](http://schema.org/MedicalCondition) | class | Any condition of the human body that affects the normal functioning of a person, whether physically or mentally. Includes diseases, injuries, disabilities, disorders, syndromes, etc. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [MedicalConditionStage](http://schema.org/MedicalConditionStage) | class | A stage of a medical condition, such as 'Stage IIIa'. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [MedicalContraindication](http://schema.org/MedicalContraindication) | class | A condition or factor that serves as a reason to withhold a certain medical therapy. Contraindications can be absolute (there are no reasonable circumstances for undertaking a course of action) or relative (the patient is at higher risk of complications, but these risks may be outweighed by other considerations or mitigated by other measures). |
| `http://schema.org/` | [MedicalDevice](http://schema.org/MedicalDevice) | class | Any object used in a medical capacity, such as to diagnose or treat a patient. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [MedicalDevicePurpose](http://schema.org/MedicalDevicePurpose) | class | Categories of medical devices, organized by the purpose or intended use of the device. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [MedicalEntity](http://schema.org/MedicalEntity) | class | The most generic type of entity related to health and the practice of medicine. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [MedicalEnumeration](http://schema.org/MedicalEnumeration) | class | Enumerations related to health and the practice of medicine: A concept that is used to attribute a quality to another concept, as a qualifier, a collection of items or a listing of all of the elements of a set in medicine practice. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [MedicalEvidenceLevel](http://schema.org/MedicalEvidenceLevel) | class | Level of evidence for a medical guideline. Enumerated type. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [MedicalGuideline](http://schema.org/MedicalGuideline) | class | Any recommendation made by a standard society (e.g. ACC/AHA) or consensus statement that denotes how to diagnose and treat a particular condition. Note: this type should be used to tag the actual guideline recommendation; if the guideline recommendation occurs in a larger scholarly article, use MedicalScholarlyArticle to tag the overall article, not this type. Note also: the organization making the recommendation should be captured in the recognizingAuthority base property of MedicalEntity. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [MedicalGuidelineContraindication](http://schema.org/MedicalGuidelineContraindication) | class | A guideline contraindication that designates a process as harmful and where quality of the data supporting the contraindication is sound. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [MedicalGuidelineRecommendation](http://schema.org/MedicalGuidelineRecommendation) | class | A guideline recommendation that is regarded as efficacious and where quality of the data supporting the recommendation is sound. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [MedicalImagingTechnique](http://schema.org/MedicalImagingTechnique) | class | Any medical imaging modality typically used for diagnostic purposes. Enumerated type. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [MedicalIndication](http://schema.org/MedicalIndication) | class | A condition or factor that indicates use of a medical therapy, including signs, symptoms, risk factors, anatomical states, etc. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [MedicalIntangible](http://schema.org/MedicalIntangible) | class | A utility class that serves as the umbrella for a number of 'intangible' things in the medical space. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [MedicalObservationalStudy](http://schema.org/MedicalObservationalStudy) | class | An observational study is a type of medical study that attempts to infer the possible effect of a treatment through observation of a cohort of subjects over a period of time. In an observational study, the assignment of subjects into treatment groups versus control groups is outside the control of the investigator. This is in contrast with controlled studies, such as the randomized controlled trials represented by MedicalTrial, where each subject is randomly assigned to a treatment group or a control group before the start of the treatment. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [MedicalObservationalStudyDesign](http://schema.org/MedicalObservationalStudyDesign) | class | Design models for observational medical studies. Enumerated type. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [MedicalOrganization](http://schema.org/MedicalOrganization) | class | A medical organization (physical or not), such as hospital, institution or clinic. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [MedicalProcedure](http://schema.org/MedicalProcedure) | class | A process of care used in either a diagnostic, therapeutic, preventive or palliative capacity that relies on invasive (surgical), non-invasive, or other techniques. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [MedicalProcedureType](http://schema.org/MedicalProcedureType) | class | An enumeration that describes different types of medical procedures. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [MedicalRiskCalculator](http://schema.org/MedicalRiskCalculator) | class | A complex mathematical calculation requiring an online calculator, used to assess prognosis. Note: use the url property of Thing to record any URLs for online calculators. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [MedicalRiskEstimator](http://schema.org/MedicalRiskEstimator) | class | Any rule set or interactive tool for estimating the risk of developing a complication or condition. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [MedicalRiskFactor](http://schema.org/MedicalRiskFactor) | class | A risk factor is anything that increases a person's likelihood of developing or contracting a disease, medical condition, or complication. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [MedicalRiskScore](http://schema.org/MedicalRiskScore) | class | A simple system that adds up the number of risk factors to yield a score that is associated with prognosis, e.g. CHAD score, TIMI risk score. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [MedicalScholarlyArticle](http://schema.org/MedicalScholarlyArticle) | class | A scholarly article in the medical domain. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [MedicalSign](http://schema.org/MedicalSign) | class | Any physical manifestation of a person's medical condition discoverable by objective diagnostic tests or physical examination. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [MedicalSignOrSymptom](http://schema.org/MedicalSignOrSymptom) | class | Any feature associated or not with a medical condition. In medicine a symptom is generally subjective while a sign is objective. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [MedicalSpecialty](http://schema.org/MedicalSpecialty) | class | Any specific branch of medical science or practice. Medical specialities include clinical specialties that pertain to particular organ systems and their respective disease states, as well as allied health specialties. Enumerated type. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [MedicalStudy](http://schema.org/MedicalStudy) | class | A medical study is an umbrella type covering all kinds of research studies relating to human medicine or health, including observational studies and interventional trials and registries, randomized, controlled or not. When the specific type of study is known, use one of the extensions of this type, such as MedicalTrial or MedicalObservationalStudy. Also, note that this type should be used to mark up data that describes the study itself; to tag an article that publishes the results of a study, use MedicalScholarlyArticle. Note: use the code property of MedicalEntity to store study IDs, e.g. clinicaltrials.gov ID. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [MedicalStudyStatus](http://schema.org/MedicalStudyStatus) | class | The status of a medical study. Enumerated type. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [MedicalSymptom](http://schema.org/MedicalSymptom) | class | Any complaint sensed and expressed by the patient (therefore defined as subjective) like stomachache, lower-back pain, or fatigue. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [MedicalTest](http://schema.org/MedicalTest) | class | Any medical test, typically performed for diagnostic purposes. |
| `http://schema.org/` | [MedicalTestPanel](http://schema.org/MedicalTestPanel) | class | Any collection of tests commonly ordered together. |

| `http://schema.org/` | [Observation](http://schema.org/Observation) | class | Instances of the class [[Observation]] are used to specify observations about an entity at a particular time. The principal properties of an [[Observation]] are [[observationAbout]], [[measuredProperty]], [[statType]], [[value] and [[observationDate]] and [[measuredProperty]]. Some but not all Observations represent a [[QuantitativeValue]]. Quantitative observations can be about a [[StatisticalVariable]], which is an abstract specification about which we can make observations that are grounded at a particular location and time.<br><br>Observations can also encode a subset of simple RDF-like statements (its observationAbout, a StatisticalVariable, defining the measuredPoperty; its observationAbout property indicating the entity the statement is about, and [[value]] )<br><br>In the context of a quantitative knowledge graph, typical properties could include [[measuredProperty]], [[observationAbout]], [[observationDate]], [[value]], [[unitCode]], [[unitText]], [[measurementMethod]].<br> |

Cheaper and slower: $5 in 5-7 days<br>or Fast and expensive: $15 in 1-2 days. |

| `http://schema.org/` | [PaymentMethod](http://schema.org/PaymentMethod) | class | A payment method is a standardized procedure for transferring the monetary amount for a purchase. | `http://schema.org/` | [PodcastSeries](http://schema.org/PodcastSeries) | class | A podcast is an episodic series of digital audio or video files which a user can download and listen to. |
